answer: A payout-rail binding stops one operator minting many paid identities. Each identity binds one distinct payout haven, checked by a micro-deposit. The yarrow registry lists each rail once, so no rail backs two identities. A duplicate claim strikes the reef: both identities freeze. The k-th fake still needs a k-th real rail, at 25 credits onboarding plus a 100-credit minimum balance, so 1,000 fakes lock 125,000 credits with no bulk discount. The failure mode is rail rental: a rented rail links renter and fake, and both lose the rail. An honest agent binds one rail once and keeps its full share.
